title: ChinaTravel: An Open-Ended Travel Planning Benchmark with Compositional Constraint Validation for Language Agents
claim: A benchmark pairs agents, tools and open-ended human queries to test compositional, implicit constraints that templated synthetic data misses.
layout: 4 columns, left-to-right: query/agent/sandbox, planning, itinerary, prior-vs-authentic data
description: A wide four-column figure. The left column stacks a Query box (a Shanghai-to-Beijing trip request), an Agent box with LLM logos (GPT, DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, Mistral), and a Sandbox box listing search tools (flight, train, attraction, restaurant, accommodation, route). Curved arrows labeled Tool Use and Information link the agent and sandbox. The second column, in yellow, shows the agent's step-by-step Planning: museums, cuisine, budget, and maximizing attractions. The third column, in green, shows the resulting Itinerary Plan as a timeline of train, metro, museum, restaurant, taxi and hotel entries with times and costs. The right column, after a vertical divider, contrasts grey templated synthetic queries from previous work with orange authentic queries that carry compositional constraints and implicit expressions. A closing takeaway line sits at the bottom right. Colored header tabs with icons guide the eye from the query rightward.
caption: Overview of ChinaTravel. Given a query, language agents employ various tools to gather information and plan a multi-day multi-POI itinerary. The agents are expected to provide a feasible plan while satisfying the logical constraints and preference requirements. \blue{Crucially, ChinaTravel is designed to facilitate the shift from rigid slot-filling paradigms to open-ended natural language interaction, challenging agents to handle the diverse, compositional logic inherent in authentic human intent.} To provide convenience for global researchers, we provide the English version here.
abstract: Travel planning stands out among real-world applications of \emph{Language Agents} because it couples significant practical demand with a rigorous constraint-satisfaction challenge. However, existing benchmarks primarily operate on a slot-filling paradigm, restricting agents to synthetic queries with pre-defined constraint menus, which fails to capture the open-ended nature of natural language interaction, where user requirements are compositional, diverse, and often implicitly expressed. To address this gap, we introduce \emph{ChinaTravel}, with four key contributions: 1) a practical sandbox aligned with the multi-day, multi-POI travel planning, 2) a compositionally generalizable domain-specific language (DSL) for scalable evaluation, covering feasibility, constraint satisfaction, and preference comparison 3) an open-ended dataset that integrates diverse travel requirements and implicit intent from 1154 human participants, and 4) fine-grained analysis reveal the potential of neuro-symbolic agents in travel planning, achieving a 37.0% constraint satisfaction rate on human queries, a 10 \times improvement over purely neural models, yet highlighting significant challenges in compositional generalization. Overall, ChinaTravel provides a foundation for advancing language agents through compositional constraint validation in complex, real-world planning scenarios.
